name: Front Insertion or Removal on an Array-Backed Sequence in a Loop
description: Elements are repeatedly added to or taken from the start of a contiguous array or list, so each operation shifts every remaining element.
extended_description: Dynamic arrays such as Python lists, JavaScript arrays, C++ vectors and Rust vectors store elements contiguously. Inserting or deleting at index zero moves all later elements, which costs time proportional to the length. Doing this once per item turns a linear pass into quadratic work, for example when a list is used as a queue.
detection_methods: Look for pop(0), insert(0, x), shift(), unshift(), erase(begin()) or remove(0) inside loops
Check whether a list or vector is being used as a FIFO queue
potential_mitigations: Use a double-ended queue such as collections.deque, std::deque or VecDeque
Iterate with an index or reverse the processing order instead of removing from the front
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Independent Async Operations Awaited One at a Time in a Loop
description: A loop starts an asynchronous request for each item and waits for it to finish before starting the next, even though the requests do not depend on each other.
extended_description: Awaiting inside a loop serialises network, disk or database calls. Total latency becomes the sum of all calls instead of roughly the slowest one. When each call is independent, starting them together with a bounded concurrency limit is usually far faster.
detection_methods: Look for await inside for, for...of or while loops whose iterations do not use each other's results
Check for .await on futures created per item inside a loop
potential_mitigations: Collect the promises or futures and await them together with Promise.all, asyncio.gather or join_all
Bound concurrency with a semaphore, p-limit or buffer_unordered where the remote side needs it
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Container Grown Element by Element Without Reserving Known Capacity
description: A buffer or vector is extended one element at a time inside a loop even though the final size is known beforehand, causing repeated reallocation and copying.
extended_description: Growable containers reallocate when they run out of room. Most grow geometrically, but each reallocation still copies the contents, and hand-written C code that grows by one element at a time copies the whole buffer on every append. When the final size is known before the loop, reserving it up front removes this work.
detection_methods: Look for realloc inside loops with a size that grows by a constant
Look for push_back or push in loops over a collection of known length with no reserve or with_capacity call
potential_mitigations: Allocate the final size once before the loop
Call reserve or with_capacity, or collect from a sized iterator
Grow buffers geometrically when the size is unknown
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Large Value Copied Where a Borrow or Reference Would Do
description: A sizeable structure, string or container is copied by value when the code only needs to read it.
extended_description: Passing or iterating large values by value duplicates their contents. In C and C++ a parameter of struct, std::vector or std::string type is copied on each call, and a range loop with a non-reference variable copies each element. In Rust, calling clone to satisfy the borrow checker inside a loop duplicates heap data that a reference would have served.
detection_methods: Check parameter types for containers, strings or large structs passed by value and only read
Look for range-based for loops with a non-reference loop variable over heavy elements
Look for .clone() inside loops where the clone is only read
potential_mitigations: Pass by const reference, pointer to const or slice
Use const auto& in range loops
Borrow with & or use Rc or Arc for shared ownership instead of cloning
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Deep Copy Through a Serialisation Round Trip
description: An object is cloned by serialising it to text or bytes and parsing it back, which is much slower than a structured copy.
extended_description: Writing an object out as JSON or pickle and immediately reading it back creates a deep copy, but pays for encoding, string allocation and parsing. It also silently drops or changes values the format cannot represent, such as dates, undefined, NaN, functions or custom classes.
detection_methods: Look for JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))
Look for pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(x)) or json.loads(json.dumps(x)) used to copy
potential_mitigations: Use structuredClone, copy.deepcopy or a purpose-built copy
Copy only the fields that will be changed
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Exceptions Thrown for Expected Outcomes Inside a Hot Loop
description: A loop signals a common, expected case such as a missing key or a non-numeric item by throwing and catching an exception on each pass.
extended_description: Raising an exception captures stack information and unwinds frames, which costs far more than a branch. When the exceptional case happens on a large share of iterations, the loop spends most of its time in exception machinery. Testing for the case first, or using a non-throwing API, avoids the cost.
detection_methods: Look for try/catch or try/except inside loops where the handler runs for routine data
Look for throw statements used to skip or end iterations
potential_mitigations: Test for the case with a lookup, parse that reports failure, or a precondition check
Use non-throwing APIs such as dict.get, std::from_chars or find
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Unbuffered Small Reads or Writes Inside a Loop
description: Data is read or written a byte, character or line at a time through an unbuffered handle, so each item costs a system call.
extended_description: System calls carry fixed overhead. Calling write, read or a synchronous file API for each small piece of data multiplies that overhead by the item count. Buffered streams, or collecting output and writing it once, reduce the number of calls by orders of magnitude.
detection_methods: Look for read or write system calls inside loops with a size of one or a few bytes
Check file handles opened without buffering and written to inside loops
potential_mitigations: Wrap handles in buffered readers or writers
Collect output in memory and write it in large blocks
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Expensive Log Message Arguments Built When the Level Is Disabled
description: A debug or trace log call formats strings, serialises objects or calls expensive functions to build its message before the logger decides to discard it.
extended_description: Most logging libraries check the level inside the log call, but the arguments are evaluated first. Building a message with string formatting, JSON serialisation or a costly helper therefore runs even when debug output is switched off. In hot paths this can dominate run time.
detection_methods: Look for f-strings, format calls, template literals or serialisation inside debug and trace log arguments
Check hot loops and request paths for verbose logging
potential_mitigations: Use the logger's lazy formatting with placeholders and arguments
Guard expensive messages with an isEnabledFor or level check
Use macros that skip argument evaluation when the level is off
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Rows Fetched Only to Count Them or Test Existence
description: All matching records are loaded from a database or API just to find out how many there are or whether any exist.
extended_description: Counting a result by loading it into memory transfers and materialises every row. The data store can return a count, or stop at the first match for an existence test, at a tiny fraction of the cost. The waste grows with table size and is often unnoticed in testing.
detection_methods: Look for len() or .length of a full query result
Look for fetchall, all() or findAll followed only by a count or emptiness test
potential_mitigations: Use COUNT, count() or an exists() query
Fetch with LIMIT 1 for an existence test
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Lock Held Across Slow I/O or an Await Point
description: A mutex or other exclusive lock stays held while the code performs network, disk or other slow operations, serialising every other thread or task that needs it.
extended_description: Locks protect shared state for short critical sections. Holding one while waiting on a remote call, a database query, a sleep or an await stretches the critical section to the length of that wait, so contending threads or tasks queue up behind it and throughput collapses under load.
detection_methods: Look for network, file, database or sleep calls between a lock acquisition and its release
Look for await expressions inside lock scopes
potential_mitigations: Copy the needed state out under the lock, release it, then do the slow work
Restructure so the slow operation does not need the lock
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Busy-Wait Polling Without Sleeping or Blocking
description: A loop repeatedly checks a flag, file, queue or time value without yielding the processor, consuming a full core while it waits.
extended_description: Spinning on a condition keeps a CPU core busy and can starve the thread that would make the condition true. It also wastes power. Waiting on a condition variable, event, channel, future or file notification, or at least sleeping between checks, lets the waiting thread use no CPU until there is work.
detection_methods: Look for while loops whose bodies only test a flag or poll a state with no sleep, wait or yield
Look for loops comparing the current time with a deadline in a tight loop
potential_mitigations: Use condition variables, events, channels, futures or OS notification APIs
Sleep or back off between polls when polling is unavoidable
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Recursive Recomputation of Overlapping Subproblems Without Memoisation
description: A recursive function calls itself on the same arguments many times along different branches and keeps no record of results, so work grows exponentially.
extended_description: Recursions such as naive Fibonacci, path counting or edit distance branch into subproblems that repeat. Without a cache, each repeated subproblem is solved again from scratch, and the call count grows exponentially with the input. Memoising results or rewriting the recursion as a table makes the work polynomial.
detection_methods: Look for functions that call themselves two or more times with overlapping argument ranges
Check whether any cache, memo table or decorator stores results
potential_mitigations: Memoise with a cache keyed by arguments, such as functools.cache
Rewrite as bottom-up dynamic programming
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Full Sequence Materialised Only to Be Scanned Once
description: An intermediate list or array is built in full and then consumed by a single pass, such as a sum, a search or an existence test, when a lazy iteration would avoid the allocation.
extended_description: Building a complete list before reducing it allocates memory proportional to the data and prevents early exit. Generator expressions, iterator chains and short-circuiting methods can compute the same answer in constant extra memory and stop at the first match.
detection_methods: Look for list comprehensions passed directly to sum, any, all, min or max
Look for filter(...).length > 0 or collect::<Vec<_>>() followed by a single iteration
potential_mitigations: Use generator expressions or iterator adaptors
Use short-circuiting methods such as some, find, any or position
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Interleaved DOM Reads and Writes Forcing Repeated Layout
description: Browser code alternates between changing styles or structure and reading layout properties inside a loop, forcing the browser to recompute layout on every pass.
extended_description: Reading properties such as offsetHeight, getBoundingClientRect or scrollTop requires up-to-date layout. If the code has just written a style or inserted a node, the browser must recalculate layout synchronously before answering. Doing this once per element turns one layout into many, a pattern often called layout thrashing.
detection_methods: Look for loops that write style or DOM changes and read layout properties in the same iteration
Check for getBoundingClientRect, offsetWidth or scrollHeight inside loops that also mutate elements
potential_mitigations: Read all layout values first, then apply all writes
Batch writes in requestAnimationFrame
Use CSS classes or transforms that avoid layout
mapping_rationale: Written for BETSY to cover a common function-level defect; not derived from an external catalog entry.

name: Large Multi-Dimensional Array Traversed Against Its Storage Order
description: Nested loops over a large two-dimensional array or matrix step the inner loop across rows instead of along them, or multiply matrices with the naive loop order, so almost every access misses the cache.
extended_description: Row-major arrays keep each row contiguous. An inner loop that varies the row index jumps a whole row per step and uses one value from each cache line it loads. The textbook triple loop for matrix multiplication reads one operand column-wise in the same way; transposing it or tiling the loops can be several times faster.
detection_methods: Find nested loops indexing a[j][i], a[k * n + i] or similar where the innermost loop variable selects the row
Find matrix multiplication written as three loops with the shared index innermost and no transposition or blocking
potential_mitigations: Swap the loops so the inner loop walks contiguous memory
Transpose one operand, tile the loops, or call a tuned linear algebra library

name: Per-Thread Data Packed Into One Cache Line and Written Concurrently
description: Threads repeatedly write to their own separate variables or array slots that sit next to each other in memory, so the shared cache line moves between cores on every write.
extended_description: Cores keep caches coherent per line, usually 64 bytes. When thread-private counters or fields share a line, each write invalidates the others' copies, and code that looks free of sharing runs slower as threads are added. This is false sharing.
detection_methods: Find arrays indexed by thread or worker id and written inside each thread's loop
Find structs whose fields are each updated by a different thread
potential_mitigations: Accumulate in a local variable and write once at the end
Pad or align per-thread slots to the cache line size

name: Shared Atomic or Locked Counter Updated on Every Iteration by All Threads
description: Worker threads update one shared atomic variable or lock-protected counter on every iteration of their main loop, so all cores contend for the same cache line and lock.
extended_description: An atomic read-modify-write needs exclusive ownership of the cache line. With several threads incrementing the same counter per item, throughput is limited by that one line, often below a single thread's speed.
detection_methods: Find fetch_add, atomic increments or locked increments of a shared variable inside per-item loops run by many threads
Check whether a per-thread local total would give the same result
potential_mitigations: Keep a local count per thread and add it to the shared value once
Use sharded or per-thread counters combined on read

name: Linked List Used for Bulk Sequential Traversal Where a Contiguous Array Would Do
description: A linked list is built and then mostly scanned or indexed from start to end, with no need for insertion or removal in the middle, so each step chases a pointer to a different part of memory.
extended_description: Linked nodes are spread over the heap and each step waits on a dependent memory load that the hardware cannot prefetch well. A contiguous array or vector holding the same data is usually several times faster to scan and uses less memory.
detection_methods: Find std::list, std::forward_list, LinkedList or hand-built node chains
Check whether the code only appends and then iterates, or indexes by position
potential_mitigations: Use a vector, Vec or array
Use a deque or an index-based structure when insertion at the ends is needed
